description: The main window. Least privilege (AGENTS.md): the app's own commands and nothing else. The job commands (D0), the browsing commands (D1), the staging commands (D2), the extract plan command (D3), the foreign-archive commands (D8: open, close, list, plan an extract; a password is sent once in the open call and kept only in Rust), the test, health, export, and repair setup commands (D4; the test and repair jobs themselves run through start_job), and the launch listener (D6: the shell's open, extract, and add verbs are handled in Rust; the webview only hears that an archive was opened or why a launch failed). The native dialogs (open, choose sources, save, choose an extract folder, choose an archive to test or repair, a copy, the new archive, a report file) are shown from Rust and dropped paths are received by Rust, so the webview never names a path: no fs, shell, http, or dialog permission is granted, and core:default is not granted. Also the passphrase and key-envelope commands (D5: unlock_archive and unlock_check_subject take a passphrase once into a zeroizing key session in Rust, cancel_unlock, list_envelopes; the create, rekey, and search jobs run through start_job). Also the update commands (T13, in-app updates: get_update_settings and set_update_settings read and change one opt-in switch, the check at start-up, which is off by default; check_for_update asks the fixed GitHub Releases endpoint, from Rust, whether a newer version exists and returns its version and release notes as text; the download and install run as the start_job kind install_update, only for the version check_for_update offered and only after the user confirms it, and the package signature is verified in Rust against the public key in tauri.conf.json before anything is installed. The webview is NOT granted any updater:* permission, makes no network request, and supplies no URL, so the CSP is unchanged.) Also open_user_guide (audit F8, Help, User guide): it takes no argument; Rust resolves the guide the installer bundles as a resource and hands it to the operating system's handler for .html, so the webview names no path and gets no fs, shell, or opener permission. The guide is static and offline.
